t.E326.agn: People have consumed soured milk and fermented products containing lactic acid for centuries. In 1974 JECFA set the ADI for potassium lactate as 'not limited'. JECFA reported that infants in their first three months have difficulty utilising DL- and D(-)-lactic acid and recommended that these forms not be used in infant foods.
t.E326.body: L(+)-lactate is a normal intermediate of mammalian metabolism and is largely converted to glycogen in the liver; the D(-) form is utilised more slowly.
t.E326.eff.0.w: Everyone except infants in their first three months
t.E326.eff.1.t: Infants in their first three months have difficulty utilising DL- and D(-)-lactic acid; JECFA recommended that these forms not be used in infant foods
t.E326.eff.1.w: Infants in their first three months
t.E326.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E326.found.1: Processed cereal-based foods and complementary foods for infants (in the EU only for pH adjustment, L(+) form)
t.E326.prod: Obtained by neutralising lactic acid; lactic acid may be produced by fermentation or by chemical synthesis.
t.E326.pw.0: JECFA has recommended that D(-)- and DL-lactic acid not be used in infant foods; in the EU, only the L(+) form is permitted in infant formulae and complementary foods for infants.
t.E326.regx.0: ADI 'not limited'; the D(-) and DL forms should not be used in infant foods.
t.E326.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E326.regx.2: In complementary foods for infants, permitted only for pH adjustment and only in the L(+) form.
t.E326.summary: The potassium salt of lactic acid. Used as an acidity regulator and humectant.
t.E326.what: The potassium salt of lactic acid, used as an acidity regulator.
